entries.title: A search branch gets an upper score
entries.lens: the exploration bonus in a search-tree selection ingredient

entries.title: Correct an off-policy sample

entries.title: Hazard accumulates into survival
entries.lens: the later segment of cumulative hazard

entries.sourceText: - **724. Bathtub curve** \[Slider\]: high early failures, a calm middle, then wear-out; tune each phase.
entries.title: Early failures and later wear

entries.sourceText: - **725. Weibull shape** \[Slider\]: shape below 1 means early failures, above 1 means wear-out.

entries.title: Compare two stipulated churn rates

entries.title: A hazard ratio bends survival

entries.title: An early advantage can reverse
entries.lens: the time-varying hazard pattern behind a crossing comparison

entries.sourceText: - **729. Log-rank test** \[Slider\]: compare two groups' survival and see how the evidence builds with more events.
entries.title: A survival contrast needs precision
entries.lens: a standardized summary rather than a full log-rank test

entries.sourceText: - **730. Competing risks** \[Slider\]: customers can cancel or downgrade; treating one as censoring overstates the other.

entries.title: The observation window starts later

entries.title: Group errors can cancel in aggregate
entries.lens: the group weights in a signed calibration-gap illustration

entries.sourceText: - **814. Abstain when unsure** \[Slider\]: let the model skip its least confident cases and watch accuracy on the rest rise.
entries.title: Abstention changes retained accuracy
entries.lens: selective retention of correct and incorrect cases

entries.sourceText: - **815. Binning tricks** \[Gotcha\]: calibration error scores change depending on how you bin predictions.
entries.title: Binning can cancel signed errors
entries.lens: the grouping weights before taking absolute calibration errors

entries.sourceText: - **816. Ask five times** \[Slider\]: sample an LLM's answer repeatedly; agreement across samples signals confidence.
entries.title: Repeated answers can agree by chance
entries.lens: the all-agree probability under independent identical answer draws

entries.sourceText: - **817. Ensemble of forecasters** \[Slider\]: averaging diverse models' probabilities improves calibration.
entries.title: Combine two forecast probabilities
entries.lens: the ensemble weights before an empirical calibration check

entries.sourceText: - **818. Superforecasters** \[Story\]: in the Good Judgment Project, aggregating top forecasters and pushing averages toward the extremes improved accuracy.
entries.title: Push aggregate odds toward extremes
entries.lens: the log-odds scaling of a forecast aggregate

entries.sourceText: - **819. Spaghetti plots** \[Slider\]: a hurricane's ensemble of possible tracks fans out over days.
entries.title: A track ensemble has growing spread
entries.lens: the stipulated forecast spread rather than a hurricane model

entries.sourceText: - **820. Honest delivery ETAs** \[Slider\]: show a range instead of a single time and watch complaints fall in a simulated app.
entries.title: An ETA range exposes uncertainty
entries.lens: the assumed arrival-time spread without a complaint-rate claim

entries.sourceText: - **822. Confidence sequences** \[Slider\]: intervals valid at every moment, so you can peek as often as you like.
entries.title: Allocate error across every look
entries.lens: the summable error budget in a Hoeffding confidence sequence

entries.sourceText: - **824. Stopped early for benefit** \[Gotcha\]: trials halted at an interim look tend to overstate the effect.
entries.title: Stopping on success selects results
entries.lens: outcome selection behind an early-stop illustration

entries.sourceText: - **825. Safe peeking vs naive peeking** \[Split\]: the same daily checks under a sequential test vs a fixed-horizon test.
entries.title: Fixed and repeated looks use budgets
entries.lens: the error allocation for a single look or all looks

entries.sourceText: - **826. Testing by betting** \[Slider\]: an e-value grows like a gambler's wealth when betting against the null.
entries.title: Evidence grows as likelihood wealth
entries.lens: the fixed-alternative likelihood ratio under a Bernoulli null

entries.sourceText: - **827. Do Bayesians care about stopping?** \[Split\]: present both sides of the optional-stopping debate with a simulation.
entries.title: Condition on the observed outcomes
entries.lens: the posterior from a proper prior under an ignorable stopping rule

entries.sourceText: - **828. Most informative question** \[Slider\]: pick the next experiment that maximizes expected information gain.
entries.title: A balanced question carries more entropy
entries.lens: the outcome entropy ingredient of information-gain design

entries.sourceText: - **829. Dose finding** \[Slider\]: place doses where they best pin down a dose-response curve.
entries.title: A dose score changes response chance
entries.lens: the response probability before calculating design information

entries.sourceText: - **830. Adaptive design** \[Slider\]: each new measurement is chosen where the model is least sure.
entries.title: Uncertainty affects an acquisition score
entries.lens: the uncertainty bonus in one adaptive measurement choice

entries.sourceText: - **831. Paired designs** \[Split\]: test each person under both conditions and noise drops sharply.
entries.title: Pairing removes shared variation
entries.lens: the covariance term in a paired mean-difference standard error

entries.sourceText: - **832. Factorial design** \[Slider\]: test 3 factors in 8 runs and read off every main effect and interaction.
entries.title: An interaction contributes to a response
entries.lens: the stipulated product contribution in a factorial illustration

entries.sourceText: - **833. Fractional factorial** \[Slider\]: halve the runs, at the cost of confusing some interactions.
entries.title: Aliased effects share a contrast
entries.lens: the unresolved mixture of two effects in a reduced design

entries.sourceText: - **834. Latin square** \[Slider\]: balance two nuisance factors, like day and machine, in one grid.
entries.title: A balanced grid has many assignments
entries.lens: the combinatorial assignment count before Latin-square restrictions

entries.sourceText: - **835. Response surface** \[Slider\]: climb toward the best settings of two factors with small designed experiments.
entries.title: A local response slope guides a move
entries.lens: one local directional slope before response-surface optimization

entries.sourceText: - **836. Power by simulation** \[Slider\]: simulate your exact design thousands of times to estimate power.
entries.title: Count significant simulated replicates
entries.lens: an illustrative rejection-count distribution under fixed power

entries.sourceText: - **837. Shared control arm** \[Slider\]: test four treatments against one control and save sample size.
entries.title: A shared control affects precision
entries.lens: the control sample size in one independent mean contrast

entries.sourceText: - **838. Ethics of adaptive allocation** \[Split\]: more patients get the better arm, but inference gets harder.
entries.title: Adaptive trial allocation changes yield
entries.lens: the reward mix before adaptive-inference corrections

entries.sourceText: - **839. Stop at enough precision** \[Slider\]: end data collection once the interval is narrow enough.
entries.title: A tighter target needs more samples
entries.lens: the normal-approximation precision target before sequential stopping

entries.sourceText: - **840. Is the test worth running?** \[Slider\]: compare the expected value of information with the cost of testing.
entries.title: A test's expected benefit meets cost
entries.lens: a supplied value-of-information benefit and testing cost

entries.sourceText: - **841. Star-rating spillover** \[Slider\]: a new rating algorithm boosts treated products' displayed stars; buyers shift from control products, so the A/B lift is mostly stolen sales. Slide the substitution rate and watch the bias grow.
entries.title: A rating lift can steal control sales
entries.lens: the control displacement inflating a measured sales contrast

entries.sourceText: - **842. Sellers react to both arms** \[Gotcha\]: when a rating formula changes, sellers adjust behavior for all buyers, contaminating control.
entries.title: Sellers change outcomes across arms
entries.lens: the cross-arm behavioral spillover in a stipulated seller model

entries.sourceText: - **843. Randomize users or items?** \[Split\]: the same rating change tested by user split and by item split gives opposite biases.
entries.title: The split changes stolen sales
entries.lens: the substitution exposure under two assumed split designs

entries.sourceText: - **844. Two-sided randomization** \[Slider\]: randomize both buyers and listings to bound the bias from each side (Johari et al., 2022).
entries.title: Both sides determine exposure
entries.lens: a two-sided exposure count before a randomization estimator

entries.sourceText: - **845. Graph cluster randomization** \[Slider\]: treat whole friend clusters so most people's friends share their arm.
entries.title: Cluster peers share treatment
entries.lens: the number of treated neighbors within an illustrative cluster

entries.sourceText: - **846. Exposure mapping** \[Slider\]: color each user by the share of treated friends and estimate effects by exposure level.
entries.title: Exposure depends on treated neighbors
entries.lens: the exposure map in a declared linear spillover model

entries.sourceText: - **847. Shared ad budgets** \[Gotcha\]: treated campaigns spend budget faster, starving control campaigns that share it.
entries.title: A shared budget can starve controls
entries.lens: the shared resource remaining after faster treatment spending

entries.sourceText: - **848. Geo experiments** \[Slider\]: randomize whole cities to measure a marketing change without spillover between users.
entries.title: Geographic separation reduces leakage
entries.lens: the cross-boundary exposure assumed in a geo design

entries.sourceText: - **850. Ratings feedback loop** \[Slider\]: higher displayed stars bring more sales, more reviews and even higher stars.
entries.title: Stars and sales can amplify each other
entries.lens: the stipulated feedback multiplier of a rating loop

entries.sourceText: - **851. Inflated ratings** \[Story\]: most Airbnb listings rate 4.5 stars or higher, compressing ratings' signal (Zervas, Proserpio & Byers, 2021).
entries.title: Compressed stars carry a smaller gap
entries.lens: the response scale of an illustrative ratings display

entries.sourceText: - **852. Herding on votes** \[Story\]: one random early upvote raised a comment's final rating about 25% on a news site (Muchnik, Aral & Taylor, 2013).
entries.title: An early vote gets amplified
entries.lens: the initial vote in a toy herding recurrence

entries.sourceText: - **853. Influence or similarity?** \[Split\]: friends behave alike because they influence each other or because they chose similar friends.
entries.title: Similarity need not mean peer influence
entries.lens: the shared-cause path in a friendship illustration

entries.sourceText: - **854. The reflection problem** \[Gotcha\]: group averages can't separate peer influence from shared circumstances (Manski, 1993).
entries.title: Peer association has a shared cause
entries.lens: the observational ambiguity of a stipulated peer model

entries.sourceText: - **855. Deworming spillovers** \[Story\]: treating children for worms also reduced infection in untreated nearby schools (Miguel & Kremer, 2004).
entries.title: An untreated neighbor can benefit
entries.lens: a positive neighborhood treatment externality in a toy model

entries.sourceText: - **856. Global vs A/B effect** \[Slider\]: the effect of launching to everyone differs from what a 50/50 test measures.
entries.title: A full rollout changes peer exposure
entries.lens: the treatment saturation behind a policy effect

entries.sourceText: - **857. Shared inventory** \[Slider\]: a pricing test sells out stock that control customers also needed.
entries.title: A test draws on shared inventory
entries.lens: the depletion rate of a common stock buffer

entries.sourceText: - **859. Shared training data** \[Gotcha\]: both arms of a recommender test feed one model, so treatment leaks into control.
entries.title: Shared training mixes treatment data
entries.lens: the data composition entering a shared model update

entries.sourceText: - **860. Cluster size trade-off** \[Slider\]: bigger clusters cut spillover bias but leave fewer units, so variance rises.
entries.title: Larger clusters leave fewer units
entries.lens: the independent-cluster count before cluster-size design effects

entries.sourceText: - **861. Front-door** \[Slider\]: with an unmeasured confounder between smoking and cancer, go through tar deposits to recover the effect.
entries.title: A mediator carries a declared path
entries.lens: the mediated coefficient under stated no-confounding assumptions

entries.sourceText: - **862. No-assumption bounds** \[Slider\]: with nothing assumed, the effect lies in an interval; watch its width (Manski, 1990).
entries.title: Unknown counterfactuals leave bounds
entries.lens: the treatment share in binary worst-case effect bounds

entries.sourceText: - **863. Add an assumption** \[Slider\]: assume monotone effects and the bounds snap tighter.
entries.title: A no-harm assumption tightens a bound
entries.lens: the monotone-response restriction on a partial identification set

entries.sourceText: - **865. Transport a trial** \[Slider\]: reweight a trial's patients to match a different target population.
entries.title: A new population changes average effect
entries.lens: the target population mix under transportable group effects

entries.sourceText: - **866. Selection diagrams** \[Slider\]: mark where two populations differ in a graph and see whether results can transfer.
entries.title: Transport needs a target composition
entries.lens: the population shift under an explicit effect-invariance assumption

entries.sourceText: - **867. Proximal inference** \[Slider\]: two imperfect proxies of a hidden confounder can together recover an effect.
entries.title: A proxy method needs identification
entries.lens: the confounding gap before a proximal bridge is identified

entries.sourceText: - **868. Negative control exposure** \[Slider\]: an exposure that can't cause the outcome but shares its confounders reveals bias.
entries.title: A negative control can reveal bias
entries.lens: the noncausal association of a declared null exposure

entries.sourceText: - **870. Truncation by death** \[Gotcha\]: comparing quality of life among survivors compares different kinds of people across arms.
entries.title: Survivors can be different people
entries.lens: outcome-dependent survival in a selected mean

entries.sourceText: - **871. Bunching at a kink** \[Slider\]: incomes pile up just below a tax threshold; the pile's size reveals how people respond to taxes.
entries.title: A threshold can change local outcomes
entries.lens: a descriptive threshold jump before structural bunching inference

entries.sourceText: - **872. Shift-share instruments** \[Slider\]: national industry shocks weighted by local industry mix create regional variation.
entries.title: Industry weights transmit shocks
entries.lens: the local exposure-weighted shift rather than instrument validity

entries.sourceText: - **873. Random judges** \[Story\]: cases randomly assigned to stricter or more lenient judges reveal effects of incarceration.
entries.title: Judge assignment supplies a first stage
entries.lens: the assumed valid-instrument ratio in a judge illustration

entries.sourceText: - **874. Mendelian randomization** \[Story\]: genes randomly inherited at conception act as instruments for exposures like alcohol use.
entries.title: A genetic instrument needs assumptions
entries.lens: the first-stage denominator under stipulated IV validity

entries.sourceText: - **875. Sensitivity contours** \[Slider\]: plot how strong a confounder must be, against treatment and outcome, to erase the estimate (Cinelli & Hazlett, 2020).
entries.title: Bias depends on two common-cause links
entries.lens: the omitted-variable contribution to an observational slope

entries.sourceText: - **876. Placebo synthetic controls** \[Slider\]: rerun synthetic control on every untreated region and see if the real effect stands out.
entries.title: A placebo gap needs a benchmark
entries.lens: the observed-minus-synthetic gap before a placebo ranking

entries.sourceText: - **877. Changes-in-changes** \[Slider\]: compare whole distributions before and after, not just means.
entries.title: A distribution has unequal group shifts
entries.lens: the quantile-group composition in a distributional contrast

entries.sourceText: - **878. Overlap weights** \[Slider\]: weight people in the region where treated and control truly overlap, avoiding extreme weights.
entries.title: Balance the region of common support
entries.lens: the balancing weight before overlap-weighted causal estimation

entries.sourceText: - **879. Trial plus real-world data** \[Slider\]: combine a small trial with a big observational dataset, letting the trial correct the bias.
entries.title: Combine a trial and a corrected estimate
entries.lens: the stipulated estimator weights after observational bias correction

entries.sourceText: - **880. Mismeasured treatment** \[Gotcha\]: if "treated" is recorded with errors, the estimated effect shrinks toward zero.
entries.title: Measurement error attenuates a slope
entries.lens: the assumed reliability factor multiplying an effect

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **881. Group-time effects** \[Slider\]: a grid of effects for each adoption cohort and each period, then aggregated (Callaway & Sant'Anna, 2021).
entries.title: Aggregate group-time effects explicitly
entries.lens: the cohort weights behind a declared causal aggregation

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **882. Clean event study** \[Slider\]: compare naive and interaction-weighted event-study plots under staggered adoption (Sun & Abraham, 2021).
entries.title: Event-study weights change the target
entries.lens: the supplied positive or negative cohort weights

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **883. Forbidden comparisons** \[Slider\]: a bar chart of the hidden 2×2 comparisons inside two-way fixed effects, including bad ones using already-treated units as controls.
entries.title: A forbidden comparison can get weight
entries.lens: the negative component in a toy fixed-effect decomposition

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **885. Synthetic diff-in-diff** \[Slider\]: weight both units and time periods to blend synthetic control with diff-in-diff (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021).
entries.title: A weighted control also has a trend
entries.lens: the control trend after unit and time weighting

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **886. Weak pre-trend tests** \[Gotcha\]: passing a pre-trend test often says little, because the test has low power (Roth, 2022).
entries.title: A noisy pretrend may look insignificant
entries.lens: the standard error behind a pretrend diagnostic

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **888. Treatment dose** \[Slider\]: diff-in-diff when regions get different intensities of a policy.
entries.title: Policy intensity changes a contrast
entries.lens: the stipulated dose slope under a parallel-trend assumption

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **889. CausalImpact** \[Slider\]: a Bayesian structural time series predicts the no-campaign path; the gap is the effect (Brodersen et al., 2015).
entries.title: A campaign gap needs a counterfactual
entries.lens: the supplied no-campaign prediction rather than fitted causal proof

entries.sourceSection: 45. Advanced diff-in-diff, synthetic control & causal time series
entries.sourceText: - **890. Seasonal interruption** \[Slider\]: model weekly and yearly cycles before estimating a policy's break.
entries.title: Seasonality belongs in the baseline
entries.lens: the common seasonal change removed by a control contrast
